headline: High-risk write and API overlap: Devin’s autonomous cloud workspace can cascade into unstructured’s document pipeline, creating default-path data leakage and action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, browser content, MCP outputs, and shared integrations; unstructured reads and writes documents. A shared workspace or document handoff lets attacker-controlled content in one agent influence the other, but no direct always-on bridge is documented, so this is below high.
conditions: IF Devin writes untrusted content into a shared repo or document that unstructured later parses
IF unstructured outputs are copied into Devin’s MCP or browser workflow without sanitization
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Devin passes any generated text to unstructured
Restrict shared folders to non-executable, non-instructional documents
Prefix all inter-agent handoffs with provenance labels
Use separate workspaces for raw inputs and agent outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If the pair shares files or integrations, sensitive material can flow from Devin into unstructured’s processing path. The profiles do not prove a default shared workspace, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF Devin places repo secrets or chat exports into a document that unstructured processes
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or document store
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared document path
Use a redaction pass before handing files from Devin to unstructured
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent
Audit uploads from Devin before document parsing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad filesystem write, Git modification, and cloud-workspace autonomy; unstructured also has filesystem write and subprocess/package installation. If both operate on the same repo or document tree, concurrent writes and Git state changes can clobber each other. The overlap is explicit and dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents are given write access to the same repository or directory
IF Devin modifies Git state while unstructured writes derived artifacts in that tree
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable Git writes for unstructured in shared repos
Run unstructured in a read-only input stage
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act in a planner-executor loop and use external integrations; unstructured transforms documents and text. If Devin’s outputs are fed into unstructured and then used as authoritative inputs for downstream actions, errors or hallucinations can propagate into commits, tickets, or messages. No verification barrier is documented, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Devin-generated text is parsed by unstructured and then forwarded to tickets, commits, or messages
IF no human or rule-based verification occurs between Devin and unstructured
mitigations: Require human approval before downstream actions
Add schema validation on Devin outputs before parsing
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Limit unstructured to extraction only, not action-taking
requires-engineering: implement verification gates in the orchestrator

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets under cloud integrations; unstructured processes documents, images, and text. If regulated or sensitive documents are routed from Devin into unstructured, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not specify matching compliance controls, so medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or secrets are placed into documents processed by unstructured
IF Devin’s integration logs retain data longer than the source system
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared processing paths
Review retention settings for both agents
Document data residency for each integration
Minimize logging of document contents
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement and audit trails
